clue.text: Dress on street giving flash regularly

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it, so the garment comes after the road

parts.note: a robe is a long loose dress or gown

explanation.surface: Someone in a striking outfit on the street sets off camera flashes again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: To strobe is to emit light in rapid repeated pulses, like a stroboscopic lamp at a disco.

clue.text: Outhouses housing right bits

indicators.note: housing means holding within, so the outbuildings take the letter for right inside them

parts.note: sheds are small outbuildings, a kind of outhouse

explanation.surface: Garden buildings containing the correct pieces of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Shreds are small torn pieces or scraps, so they are synonyms of bits.

clue.text: Inhibition of one in holiday rave

parts.note: a rest is a break or holiday from work

indicators.note: in places the numeral for one within the word for a tirade

parts.note: to rant or rave is to talk wildly; a rant is a tirade
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone at a holiday party wonders who among them is holding back.
explanation.definitionFit: Restraint is self-control that holds back feelings or actions, the same idea as an inhibition.

clue.text: Bird is damaged lying on a road

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece lying on others sits above them, so it comes first

parts.note: bust is informal for broken or damaged

explanation.surface: An injured bird lies in the middle of a road.
explanation.definitionFit: The bustard is a large heavy ground-dwelling bird of open country, so it is one example of a bird.

clue.text: Positions sculptor's head cutting into sculptures

indicators.note: cutting into means pushing inside, so the opening letter goes within the word for carved figures

parts.note: statues are carved or cast sculptures

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, here of the word for the artist

explanation.surface: An artist's head pokes into a gallery of sculptures, like a curious visitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Statuses are standings or ranks within a group, so they are positions in a hierarchy.

clue.text: Splutter over getting clues

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, so read the word for splutter backwards

parts.note: to spit is to splutter out words or spray saliva

explanation.surface: Someone splutters on being handed the hints to a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Tips are helpful hints or pointers, which is what clues provide.

clue.text: Foreign capital excursion on oil rig, occasionally

indicators.note: in a down clue the trip sits on top of the selected letters, so it comes first

parts.note: a trip is a short excursion or outing

indicators.note: occasionally means taking only some letters, here every other one of the oil-rig words

explanation.surface: A sightseeing trip to a foreign city made from an offshore oil platform now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is the capital city of Libya, so to a British solver it is a capital abroad.

clue.text: Broke surface on top of tapioca

indicators.note: in a down clue the surface layer sits on what follows, so it comes first

parts.note: the skin is the outer surface layer, as on a milk pudding

indicators.note: the top of a down-written word is its opening letter, here of the pudding word

explanation.surface: The skin forming on top of a bowl of tapioca pudding breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broke' reads as a verb about the pudding skin cracking, but it is the adjective meaning penniless. SKINT is British slang for having no money.
explanation.definitionFit: Skint is British slang for having no money, the same sense as broke meaning penniless.

clue.text: Abuse me sternly employing academic term

indicators.note: employing means the phrase uses the letters within it, so the term sits inside the words abuse me sternly

explanation.surface: A teacher is told off harshly for using some academic jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: A semester is one of the halves into which a college year is divided, a period of teaching.

clue.text: Fight excess swallowing small single

indicators.note: swallowing means taking in, so the word for the surplus closes round the two letters

parts.note: the rest is what is left over, the surplus or excess
S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
I is the Roman numeral one, a single

explanation.surface: An instruction to fight overindulgence by gulping down one small thing.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to oppose or struggle against something, so it is a synonym of fight.

clue.text: Work period cut one's minute hope

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: cut means a piece is docked, here the final letter of the word for a period

parts.note: time is a period or spell
one's is read as one is, I + S

explanation.surface: Someone whose working hours have been shortened clings to a tiny hope.
explanation.walkthrough: One's is taken as 'one is', which gives I (the Roman one) plus S.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimism is a hopeful confidence that things will turn out well, so it is close to hope.

clue.text: Rubbish celebrity practically pocketing shedloads

indicators.note: pocketing means putting inside, so the shortened renown word holds the large quantity
practically means almost, so the word for renown loses its final letter

parts.note: fame is celebrity, being widely known
shedloads is slang for a great quantity, lots

explanation.surface: A worthless celebrity is stuffing huge amounts of money into their pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: Flotsam is floating wreckage or debris, extended to mean worthless odds and ends.

clue.text: Bar overturned before charge at the back

indicators.note: before places the reversed bar ahead of the charge
overturned means the word for bar is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: a rod is a metal bar
a sally is a sudden charge out of a besieged position, a sortie

explanation.surface: A barrier is knocked over just ahead of a cavalry charge from the rear.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorsally means on or towards the dorsal side, the back of an animal's body, as opposed to its belly.

clue.text: Stands? Hard in wellies, perhaps!

indicators.note: in places the letter for hard within the footwear word

parts.note: wellingtons are an example of boots, hence the perhaps
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about standing up, answered by being firm in rubber boots.
explanation.walkthrough: Wellies are wellington boots, British rubber rain boots.
explanation.definitionFit: Booths are small stalls or kiosks at a fair or market, so they are stands in that sense.

clue.text: Hard old lady with Italian sweetheart

parts.note: gran is a grandmother, an informal old lady
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter

explanation.surface: An elderly woman out with her Italian lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetheart' looks like a lover but splits as 'sweet heart': the middle letter of SWEET.
explanation.definitionFit: Granite is a very hard igneous rock, used figuratively for something unyielding, so it stands for hard.

clue.text: Vague tirade with eminent lunatic …

indicators.note: lunatic means crazy, so the letters of the two words are rearranged wildly

explanation.surface: A rambling outburst delivered by a distinguished but crazed figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Indeterminate means not precisely fixed or known, the same idea as vague or uncertain.

clue.text: Hires out a buggy getting permit

indicators.note: buggy means full of faults, so the letters of the phrase are scrambled

explanation.surface: A hire firm rents out a pram or cart and must obtain a licence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buggy' looks like the vehicle being hired out, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To authorise is to give official approval, so it means to permit.

clue.text: Journalist is on drink

parts.note: re means on or about, as in correspondence
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: A newspaper writer is on the booze.
explanation.definitionFit: A reporter gathers and writes news stories, so is a kind of journalist.

clue.text: … natter with eminent lunatic provides amusement

indicators.note: lunatic means crazy, so the letters of the chat word and the distinguished word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: chatting with the same mad dignitary is quite amusing.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to 15-across, which used the same indicator and the same word eminent.
explanation.definitionFit: Entertainment is anything that diverts or delights people, which is what amusement means.

clue.text: Strains to produce puzzles

definitions.meaning: to riddle is to pass soil or gravel through a coarse sieve, so it strains

explanation.surface: Effort is needed to come up with brainteasers.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle is both a coarse sieve, used as a verb for straining, and a puzzling question.

clue.text: Undoing blouse embracing masculine clot

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the rearranged garment wraps round the letter
undoing means unfastening and so disordering, so the letters of the garment are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man is hugged while someone unbuttons a blouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Undoing' rearranges BLOUSE to EBOLUS; 'embracing' then puts M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An embolus is a blood clot or other mass lodged in a blood vessel, causing a blockage.

clue.text: If not overcast, taking top off

indicators.note: taking the top off a down entry removes its first letter

parts.note: an overcast sky is sunless

explanation.surface: On a cloudy day, should you strip off?
explanation.definitionFit: Unless is a conjunction meaning except if, so it stands in for if not.

clue.text: In agreement negotiating is done

indicators.note: negotiating means working through or round, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: Parties have reached agreement because the deal is finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Onside is informal for supportive or agreeing, as in getting colleagues on side.

clue.text: Streak in street with breeze rising

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: a breeze is a movement of air

explanation.surface: A streak of something seen in the street as the wind picks up.
explanation.definitionFit: A stria is a thin line, groove or stripe on a surface, such as a stretch mark, so a streak.

clue.text: Inflexible end delivered

parts.note: a stub is the short end left over, as of a cigarette
a baby delivered is born

explanation.surface: A baby that refuses to bend, finally brought into the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubborn means obstinately refusing to change, so it is unyielding or inflexible.

clue.text: Sort of immunity is caught, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word for caught is spoken, and something sounding the same is entered

parts.note: to catch what someone says is to hear it

explanation.surface: A pandemic-era remark about which kind of immunity is picked up, according to reports.
explanation.definitionFit: Herd immunity is protection across a population once enough individuals are immune, so the word names a kind of immunity.

clue.text: Tweeted about husband becoming excited

indicators.note: about means around, so the birdsong word goes round the letter for husband

parts.note: a bird that tweets trills

explanation.surface: Someone posted online about their spouse becoming delighted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tweeted' suggests social media, but it is birdsong.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrilled means feeling a sudden wave of excitement or delight, a strong form of excited.

clue.text: Spot, we hear, to find fish

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for spot is spoken, and a word sounding the same is entered

parts.note: a spot is a place or location

explanation.surface: An angler looks for a good location to catch fish, on local advice.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaice is a flatfish of European seas with orange spots, so it is an example of a fish.

clue.text: Ecstatic feeling from, perhaps, Odyssey

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the run of words perhaps and Odyssey

explanation.surface: A reader feels elation from a great epic such as Homer's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' looks like it marks the Odyssey as an example, but it is part of the hidden letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhapsody is a state of rapturous delight or enthusiasm, an ecstatic feeling.

clue.text: Idiots accepting leader of Tories' qualities

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the word for fools holds that letter

parts.note: asses are fools or idiots

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of the party word

explanation.surface: Fools take on board what is good about the Conservative leadership.
explanation.walkthrough: Tories are members of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets are useful or valuable attributes, so they are good qualities.
